name: myself.md
tagline: Give your AI the phone data you choose to share
description: Use health, screen-time and recorded location data in your AI workflow. Choose data types and date ranges in export profiles, then approve what compatible agents can read through MCP. Browse the fictional dashboard demo without signing in. Private reads require a paired phone and your approval. Supported data varies by platform; public mobile store downloads are coming soon.
suggestedPricing: Paid with a free trial or plan
firstComment:
Hi Product Hunt, I'm Cody, the maker of myself.md.

myself.md lets you bring selected phone records into your AI workflow. You create an export profile with the data types and date range you want, then approve what a compatible agent can read through MCP.

For example, you could ask your agent to summarize your step counts and app usage for the past week. The agent requests the approved records; phone support and OS permissions determine which data is available. You can also export to local files, your own HTTPS endpoint, or the paired cloud service.

Try the dashboard at https://myself.md/demo. It uses fictional records and requires no account. Public mobile store downloads are coming soon. The gallery shows the current iPhone interface with an isolated sample profile, including data selection and the separate agent-permission confirmation.

Cloud exports are encrypted at rest, and the service decrypts approved reads. Revoking sharing stops future reads; it can't recall copies already sent to an AI provider.

I'd like to hear which records you'd use first, and what you'd want to check before giving an agent access.
